refnamediv.refpurpose: Collect and evaluate platform authentication state

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: platformd-trustd.service collects boot, login session, user identity, and authentication evidence. It evaluates named local policies and can produce TPM attestation over the collected state.
The service does not authenticate users, process credentials, release secrets, or grant access. A caller that consumes a policy result remains responsible for enforcement.

Boot information is obtained from EFI variables, the TPM PCR bank, and the TCG event log. Session state is obtained from systemd-logind.service8. User records are resolved through the User/Group Record Lookup API. Authentication events are submitted over Varlink by privileged local components.
The daemon sends a readiness notification and terminates on SIGTERM or SIGINT.

refsect1.title: Session state
refsect1.para: Session lock state is read from the logind LockedHint property. It is reported as locked, unlocked, or unknown. Lock state changes do not establish or clear verification freshness.

New sessions have no verification timestamp. Session creation and unlock notifications do not establish freshness. Freshness is established only by an accepted event with pamService set to platformd-verify, phase set to verify, declaredMethod set to platformd-verify, and result set to success. The event must name an existing eligible logind session owned by the declared user ID.
Freshness uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME, has a default window of 300 seconds, and is cleared before suspend. The window may be set with $PLATFORMD_TRUST_FRESH_WINDOW_SEC.

refsect1.title: Varlink interface
refsect1.para: The service listens on /run/platformd-trustd/io.platformd.Trust and implements io.platformd.Trust. The interface contains methods for reading boot, session, identity, authentication event, and runtime measurement records. It also contains methods for evaluating policies and producing attestation.

SubmitAuthEvent requires a caller with user ID 0. It validates field lengths and values, the declared user name and user ID, the named session, and session ownership. Records from pam_platformd.so use the session phase and are audit records only. They do not establish freshness.
The attestation methods also require user ID 0. Reading collected state and evaluating a policy do not require privilege. No secret or PAM response is carried by the interface.

refsect1.title: Policies
refsect1.para: verified-boot succeeds when PCR 11 matches a provisioned local reference. fresh-user-verification requires an active and unlocked eligible session with a qualifying verification inside the freshness window. local-trusted-session additionally requires a local session, a verified user record, and a verified-local boot.
Each result includes a stable machine-readable reason code and a descriptive reason. The result is policy-satisfied or denied.

refsect1.title: Evidence and attestation
refsect1.para: The boot is reported as verified-local when PCR 11 matches a reference generated from an installed unified kernel image by systemd-measure1. The references are maintained by a kernel-install8 plugin. They are local reference values and do not establish an external trust root.

When TPM support is available, Attest returns a nonce-bound quote over the boot PCRs. Runtime events are extended into a TPM NV index. GetAttestationToken combines the quote, boot measurements, and runtime log in the JSON Entity Attestation Token profile. GetEnrollment and ActivateCredential support binding the attestation key to the TPM.
Authentication events are declared evidence. TPM measurement protects the recorded sequence from undetected modification after collection, but does not verify a declared authentication method.
